name: Vitamin C and zinc pit routine

lead: This routine is an informal approach to underarm odor that people in grooming circles describe, using topical or dietary vitamin C and zinc to smell fresher.

Underarm odor is generally attributed to skin bacteria breaking down apocrine sweat into smelly compounds, and the idea is that these ingredients curb that process. The practice is anecdotal, and no published studies of this specific routine were located.

paras: People add vitamin C and zinc to their underarm care, either as a product applied after washing or through diet, alongside regular washing and deodorant. Users describe judging results by how their odor changes over days to weeks.
No specific harms are documented for the routine itself, though any topical product can irritate sensitive underarm skin. Persistent odor can have medical causes, and a clinician can check for them.

chain: Vitamin C and zinc on underarms
angle.text: Users apply or take vitamin C and zinc hoping to reduce the odor-causing bacteria under the arms and smell fresher around others. The routine is anecdotal and no studies of it were located.

lead: The "vitamin C and zinc pit routine" is an informal underarm-care practice discussed in grooming circles as a way to manage body odor, typically involving topical or dietary vitamin C and zinc. It is described as anecdotal, and no published studies of this specific routine were located.
Background on how underarm odor arises is available: bacteria on the skin break down apocrine sweat secretions into odorous compounds, and genetics, diet and health also influence odor.[1]

paras: Body odor is attributed mainly to skin bacteria acting on apocrine sweat in the armpits, with variation linked to genes such as ABCC11.[1] Established approaches described include antibacterial soap, deodorant and antiperspirant.[1]
